subject: environmental-science

moments.title: Stockholm Conference
moments.body: The UN Conference on the Human Environment, 5-16 June 1972, is the first major UN conference on international environmental issues. 113 nations attend. The Stockholm Declaration (26 principles) and an action plan emerge. UNEP (UN Environment Programme) is created, headquartered in Nairobi.
moments.takeaway: The international environmental governance architecture in active use today began with one conference in Sweden in 1972.

now.title: International environmental governance today
now.body: UNEP coordinates global environmental policy, hosts MEAs (Multilateral Environmental Agreements), and produces the annual Emissions Gap Report. The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (1992), CBD (1992), UNCCD (1994) and successors all trace lineage to Stockholm.
now.open_questions: Can fragmented MEAs evolve into coherent Earth system governance? IPBES (biodiversity, 2012) and other panels increasingly try to link them.

reflection: Indira Gandhi's Stockholm speech argued: 'Are not poverty and need the greatest polluters?' The development-vs-environment tension framed at Stockholm runs through every subsequent COP and SDG negotiation.
